newsitem.title: UK: Scor shares sold widely in market-analysts.
newsitem.headline: Scor shares sold widely in market-analysts.

text.p: Large shareholdings in French reinsurer Scor have been sold into the market and not to trade buyers, analysts said on Friday after news that AXA and AGF had between them sold almost 20 percent of the company's share capital in recent months.
"It's just generally going into the market. It's certainly not a trade buyer," said one insurance analyst.
Volume in Scor, which has 22 million shares outstanding, has been heavy since March, with around 750,000 shares changing hands on Wednesday and daily volume regularly topping 500,000.
"All of it isn't just AXA and AGF, but it's believable to me that a significant amount of stock did go through the market," said Salomon Brothers London-based insurance analyst Brian Shea.
Industry sources said market buyers included a German investment fund and a life insurance unit of French mutual bank Credit Agricole, which had bought around 2.0 percent.

Interest in the shares has been fuelled by their recent outperformance of other French insurance stocks and supported by speculative buying sparked by a flurry of takeover activity in the international reinsurance sector.
On Tuesday, Swiss Re acquired M&G Re from Prudential hard on the heels of Munich Re's $3.3 billion acquisition of American Re earlier in August and General Re 's purchase of National Re in July.
Scor itself bought Allstate's reinsurance business in July. However, analysts played down speculation that Scor might become a takeover target, while not ruling out the prospect altogether.
"I don't see anybody committing anything. I think it's reasonable to assume that AXA and AGF would have offered their stakes to a trade buyer before going to the market with them," Shea said.
"Anyone who's remotely interested in buying Scor would have known this for more than six months now," he added.
Another London-based analyst agreed that buying was driven by investors looking for value.

"This is the market buying Scor on the basis that it is still desperately cheap relative to the U.S. reinsurers, relative to Swiss Re and M&G. I don't think there's anything more to it than that at this stage."

Axa said earlier it had sold its full 9.7 percent stake and that was followed by an announcement from fellow French insurer Assurances Generales de France that it had disposed of nine percent of its 9.71 percent stake in Scor, the country's leading reinsurer.
The AGF shares were sold at an average price of 204.50 francs, net of brokerage fees, and the sales were staggered over the period since its privatisation in May.

The timing of AFG and AXA's exit was probably connected to the expected sale of shares by Scor's largest shareholder, UAP, to avoid a sudden glut which would have depressed the share price, French analysts said.

Both insurers made clear earlier in the year they planned to reduce their holdings in Scor. Union des Assurances de Paris today repeated its intention to cut its 40.9 percent stake when Scor lists in New York, a move expected this autumn, probably September.

"If UAP comes out, you have a genuinely independent company. Therefore in theory it could become a target. In theory. But I suspect the market is saying the ownership structure has been one of the handicaps the stock has laboured under," one London-based analyst said.
The value of shares in Scor, which announced in June it would list its shares on the New York Stock Exchange by year-end, has climbed by more than 33 percent since the start of the year.
"Scor shares are attractive on the basis that they are clearly undervalued. That is irrespective of any whiff of corporate activity," the analyst added.

Other analysts noted that Scor was big enough to stand on its own feet as an independent reinsurer, adding that the French government would be reluctant to see the company snapped up by a foreign buyer.
One Paris-based analyst said a link-up with an insurer of a similar size to Scor was more likely than a takeover by a big reinsurer.
Scor shares closed up two francs at 206 and analysts in Paris and London believe the shares are set to head towards 250 to 270 francs.
-- John Sanders, Reuters Insurance News 44 171 542 2769
